updates.previous: SBA 7(a) standard acquisition: 10% cash equity injection, 10% seller note on full standby, 80% SBA loan at prime + 2.5–3% over 10 years. Target a business priced $500K–$1.5M with verified SDE of $150K–$400K.
updates.proposed: At least one lender now requires 15% cash equity injection on deals over $500K, with no seller note credit toward it regardless of standby terms. This raises minimum cash-to-close and shrinks the executable deal size for a $120K cash buyer — likely capping deals near $800K rather than $1.2M+. Need to confirm whether this is lender-specific or an industry-wide shift by shopping additional lenders.
updates.reason: New lender guidance materially changes the cash injection assumption the entire plan is built on, directly affecting deal size ceiling for the user's stated $120K cash position.

updates.previous: Recommended $700K–$1.5M, requires $100–175K liquid all-in, assuming seller note can offset half the cash injection.
updates.proposed: With $120K cash and a lender requiring 15% cash (no seller-note credit) on deals over $500K, max supportable deal size is roughly $800K (15% = $120K) unless a lender without this requirement is found. Sub-$500K deals may still allow the old 10%/seller-note structure. Deal size ceiling needs re-modeling against both lender types.
updates.reason: New lender term directly changes the math behind the recommended deal size range for this specific user's capital.

updates.previous: If your background doesn't qualify, you need a partner or a business with an existing GM before lender conversations are productive.
updates.proposed: New blocking issue: the user's intended partner will not sign a personal guarantee. Since SBA 7(a) requires unlimited personal guarantees from all 20%+ owners, this partner cannot be a co-owner/co-borrower under the current structure. Must clarify whether the partner is meant to be a guarantor, a minority non-owner, an operating-only partner, or excluded from the deal structure entirely — this affects both experience-documentation strategy and equity structure.

updates.previous: Personal guarantee exposes all personal assets for the full 10-year loan term — mitigation: discuss with a financial advisor and family members who share assets.
updates.proposed: New risk: if a partner is involved in the deal (financially or operationally) but refuses to sign a personal guarantee, this could disqualify them from being a 20%+ equity owner under SBA rules, or could force the user to hold guarantee liability alone while sharing upside — a structural/legal question needing attorney input before proceeding with any partner-based deal structure.
